title: Lights out
question: How few doorways can you get away with?
rules_on_image: Step into a room and its light flips: on turns off, off turns on.
Stepping out changes nothing. Reuse rooms and doorways freely.
Start in the Hall. Leave by the back door with every light off.
Count every pass through an inside doorway. The back door doesn't count.

difficulty.assessed: Hard (lower end) per Claude; Medium per independent blind solve (Codex gpt-6-astra, 322 s)
difficulty.assessed_by: Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5); independent blind solve by Codex recorded in qa-report.md; no human test
difficulty.rationale: Requires the entry-parity insight (lit rooms odd entries, dark rooms even), the start-room and end-room traps, unavoidable dark rooms costing two entries, a forced visiting order, and a counting proof that 13 is minimal.

x_caption: Every room you walk into flips its light. How few doorways does it take to leave by the back door with the whole house dark?

solution.proof_summary: Doorways = room entries. Lit rooms need an odd number of entries, dark rooms an even number. Five lit rooms (Hall included) need at least 1 each; Office, Library and Kitchen are unavoidable dark rooms needing 2 each; the dark Boot room must be finished in, so needs 2. 5 + 6 + 2 = 13, and the route above achieves it.
